title: Authorization Token v1.1 — Scope Token claim set
description: The gatekeeper Scope Token JWT payload (doc 01 §5.5 as amended by Ruling A, converged with doc 11 §3.2; Ruling C5: the ONLY execution credential). Header is always {"alg": "EdDSA", "typ": "JWT", "kid": "gk-…"} — Ed25519, verified against gatekeeper's JWKS (cached ≤ 5 min, two active keys max, kid rotation). Rules not expressible statically (enforced by token-service/PEP): exp − iat ≤ 900 s (15-min TTL for ALL active classes R1–R3); no unauthenticated refresh — long-running work re-authorizes mid-run via the SDK/PEP; tokens are task-bound (jti reuse across tasks = anomaly + auto-revocation); mTLS workload identity is required IN ADDITION to the token; R2/R3 tokens always use the exact-enumerated target manifest; nbf verified with 60 s leeway, skew > 120 s rejected.

jti.description: Token id (ULID). This is the authorization_token_id carried by AlertEvent v1 producers (doc 05 §5.2).

sub.description: Subject — the executing agent/workload, e.g. "agent_01J92F…" or "svc-stress-engine".

task_id.description: Task this token is bound to — single-purpose, useless for any other task.

roe_version.description: RoE version the token binds to; PEPs re-validate and halt on version/expiry change.

risk_class.description: Authorized risk class. Tokens are minted only for active classes R1–R3; R0 requires no per-target token (doc 11 §1).

targets.description: Hashed target manifest reference (doc 01 §5.5). Exact-enumerated form: manifest holds the concrete target list. Scope-bound watch-token form (scope_bound=true): manifest holds the canonical RoE scope document and manifest_sha256 IS the "scope:sha256:<hash>" audit value (Ruling A.3).

count.description: Number of concrete targets (exact-enumerated form; omitted for scope-bound).

scope_bound.description: Ruling A extension — the scope-bound watch-token form. Valid ONLY for the R1 standing capabilities monitor.watch / monitor.rescan (see allOf below). When true, the SDK/PEP evaluates each probe target against the manifest's embedded canonical scope (domains, CIDRs, exclusions) using doc 01 §10.1's canonicalized matching (longest-prefix/exact-host); EXCLUSIONS ALWAYS WIN; fail-closed — a scan job without a valid in-scope token is dead-lettered and audit-logged.

rate_caps.description: Self-contained rate caps enforced by the PEP per burst — the token is NOT a capability to bypass rate limits (doc 11 §3.2). doc 01 §5.5 form {"max_rps": 50}; doc 11 §3.2 form {"rps": 5000, "max_concurrent": 2} — max_rps ≡ rps, one claim set.

approval_id.description: Four-eyes approval reference ("appr_…") — mandatory for R3 and for R2 stress.* on production targets (Ruling B.4).

nbf.description: Not-before (Unix seconds; 60 s leeway on verification).

exp.description: Expiry (Unix seconds) — exp − iat ≤ 900 (15-min TTL, Ruling C5), enforced by token-service at mint.

allOf.description: scope_bound=true is valid ONLY for the R1 standing capabilities monitor.watch / monitor.rescan (Ruling A.1, A.2).
Four-eyes approval reference is mandatory for R3 (doc 01 §5.5, Ruling B.4). The R2 stress.*-on-production case is enforced by policy-service step 7 (needs target context, not statically checkable).
